title: The Pending Signature

people.name: Elena Blackwood
people.personality: Sir Edmund's only child, motherless since girlhood and raised by her father to inherit the house. Proud, restrained and entirely self-possessed. Cool and formal, never familiar; speaks in complete, firm sentences, seeks no sympathy and never apologises. Under pressure she demands precision, and never raises her voice or stoops to insult. Says ‘let me be perfectly clear’ and ‘don't twist my words’, and cuts any insinuation dead.

people.name: Victor Hale
people.personality: A country doctor who has attended the Blackwoods for years and served in a field hospital during the war. Reserved, analytical and outwardly cold. Formal in address; carefully separates what he observed from what he surmises, and corrects the question before answering it. Brief, exact, almost clinical phrasing. Says ‘let us be precise’, ‘let us keep to the facts’ and ‘one must distinguish’, and never ventures a diagnosis he cannot defend.

people.name: Clara Reed
people.personality: Handles Sir Edmund's correspondence, diary and papers; she came to the house with a letter of reference and no fortune but her wages. Observant, prudent and direct. Polite and formal in address, prefers plain words and always separates what she knows from what she supposes. Doesn't apologise every other sentence. Under pressure she clings to verifiable details. Says ‘I'll put it plainly’ and ‘that's what I can tell you’.

people.name: Arthur Finch
people.personality: Thirty years in Sir Edmund's service; he knows every habit of the house. Formal, discreet and dry, trained in the old school. Never familiar, and addresses whoever questions him as ‘sir’. Answers point by point, in orderly sentences with no visible emotion. Under pressure he keeps his courtesy without sliding into servility. Never speculates about the family or the rest of the staff, and closes a subject with ‘that is all on that point’.

people.name: Julian Blackwood
people.personality: Sir Edmund's nephew; lives on an allowance his uncle never let him forget, and spends more time in London than at the house. Impatient, defensive and proud in his own way. Casual with everyone, the detective included: no titles, no ceremony. Talks in short, colloquial sentences, straight out, and hates being credited with more than he said. Under pressure he turns curt, never violent. Says ‘look, listen’, ‘I'll tell you straight’ and ‘don't make a meal of it’.

rooms.name: Study
rooms.description: Dark oak panelling, a mahogany desk with a green leather top and a brass lamp that leaves the rest of the room in half-light. It smells of pipe tobacco and ink, and the rain beats ceaselessly on the closed windows.
ambience: As you enter, you feel the chill of the dead fireplace and hear the tick of a mantel clock nobody has looked at in hours. The leather armchairs creak at the slightest movement.
The brass lamp casts a green circle on the desk top and leaves the rest in shadow. The windows shudder at every gust, and the smell of stale tobacco clings to your clothes.

rooms.name: Library
rooms.description: Walnut shelves climb to a gallery with a turned wooden railing, reached by a wrought-iron spiral staircase. It smells of old leather and paper, and the fire in the grate barely reaches the highest spines.
ambience: As you enter, the parquet creaks under your shoes and the sound rises to the gallery, where it is lost among the books. The flames crackle, small and stubborn.
Here the silence is thick and muffles the rain. It is colder up above than down below, and now and then the iron staircase gives a faint tick, as if cooling.

rooms.name: Dining room
rooms.description: A long mahogany table beneath a crystal chandelier, the silver still laid out in rows, and ancestral portraits gazing down from the walls. The air still holds a smell of candle wax, roast lamb and port.
ambience: As you enter, the chandelier's crystals tinkle in the draught rising from the hall. The portraits seem to follow you with their eyes, stern and bored.
The candles have burned halfway down and the wax hangs in tears from the silver candelabra. The rain lashes the tall windows like flung gravel.

rooms.name: Kitchen
rooms.description: An iron range still warm, copper pans hung in a row and a pine table scrubbed almost white. It smells of strong tea, bread and coal, and rainwater gurgles in the drain out in the yard.
ambience: As you enter, you are met by a warmth found nowhere else in the house. A tabby cat dozes by the range, and the wall clock moves on with a dry, domestic tick.
The bells on the board, one for each room, hang motionless above the door. It smells of soda soap and of washing hung to dry near the fire.

rooms.name: Conservatory
rooms.description: Misted glass, terracotta pots and fleshy-leaved plants thriving in a damp, sticky heat. Violet-blue flowers peep out among the ferns, and the rain drums on the glass dome.
ambience: As you enter, the hot air dampens your face all at once. It smells of wet earth and sap, and a drop of condensation slides down the back of your neck.
Beneath the dome the roar of the rain is so constant that it comes to feel like silence. The palm fronds stir faintly, though there is not a breath of air.

rooms.name: Hall
rooms.description: A chequered marble floor, an oak staircase climbing into darkness and a longcase clock that strikes the quarters with a deep chime. It smells of wet coats and furniture polish, and the wind creeps in under the front door.
ambience: As you enter, the echo of your footsteps rings off the marble and climbs the stairs. The umbrellas in the stand drip unhurriedly onto a brass tray.
A cold draught comes down from the top of the stairs and sets the lamps flickering. The stag antlers cast shadows like bare branches on the panelling.

crime.phrase: by poisoning him with aconite in the teacup
crime.motive: Had received an order, signed by her father, cutting her out of the inheritance the next day, and had signed the acknowledgement of receipt.

opening.arrival: You are received in the hall, your coat still dripping, and shown to the study, where the master of the house lies beside his desk. On the green leather lie half-sorted papers and an uncapped pen, as though a signature had been left for the morrow.
opening.tension: Something was to be signed in this house in the morning, and someone could not allow it. With the bridge under water nobody will leave before dawn, and everyone already has a rehearsed account of where they were.

night: The rain beats harder against the panes and the wind begins to whistle in the chimneys. In the hall, the longcase clock goes on striking the quarters, unhurried.
In the kitchen someone puts the kettle on again; nobody in the house means to go to bed. Footsteps in the corridors stop, then move away again.
A long roll of thunder rumbles over the countryside and the lamps flicker for an instant. The maids hand out candles along the passages, in case the lights fail.
The river keeps rising: from the upper windows the water can be seen gleaming where the meadow used to be. Nobody mentions the bridge any more.
The candles have burned down to stubs and the house smells of cold smoke. Upstairs, a door closes far too softly.
The storm is at its worst: shutters bang and the fires shrink in the grates. Everyone waits, and nobody dares look at the others.
epilogue: {p1} hears the accusation without interrupting. At the end there is only a request for a glass of water, and it is the housekeeper who brings it, without a word, on the silver tray kept for great occasions. {p1}'s hands shake taking it. Nobody else moves. There is not a whole candle left in the house when, shortly before dawn, the cocks on the farms begin to crow and the water stops beating on the panes. By mid-morning the village sergeant crosses the bridge in muddy boots and leads {p1} away down the oak avenue.

clues.title: Teacup
clues.text: {victim}'s cup contains aconite. {p1}'s fingerprint lies over the residue on the inner rim: she handled the cup after the poison was in it.

clues.title: Preliminary report
clues.text: {victim} was found in {r1}. No wounds: aconite poisoning, swallowed at 21:15. He remained in this room until his death at 21:30.

clues.title: Inheritance papers
clues.text: An order signed by {victim} cutting {p1} out of the inheritance the next day. At the foot, the acknowledgement of receipt, signed by {p1}.

clues.title: Medical accounts
clues.text: A corrected total, signed by {p2} and accepted by {victim}. There are no fictitious medical fees.

clues.title: Botanical treatise
clues.text: Aconite may be swallowed dissolved in tea or in wine alike. Symptoms appear after about ten minutes.

clues.title: {p3}'s correspondence
clues.text: An application for another post, drafted by {p3}. Her ties to {victim} were purely professional.

clues.title: Glasses examined
clues.text: The wine glasses hold no poison. The tainted drink was the tea.

clues.title: After-dinner photograph
clues.text: {p1} and {p5} appear in {r3} at 21:00. The picture does not prove where they were at 21:15.

clues.title: {p5}'s correspondence
clues.text: {p5} owed {victim} money and was arranging the sale of a family jewel. The sale had not yet gone through.

clues.title: Service tray
clues.text: {p4} made the tea at 21:05. {p1} took the cup from {r4} at 21:12 and carried it into {r1} at 21:15. {victim} drank it there.

clues.title: Medicine-chest bottle
clues.text: Aconite concentrate, kept in the household medicine chest. The bottle bears no name: by itself it does not show who used it.

clues.title: Servants' register
clues.text: {p4}'s request to retire, not yet dealt with. There is no record of money being diverted.

clues.title: Aconite plant
clues.text: The plant is untouched: nobody has cut a stem tonight. Analysis traces the poison to the preparation in the medicine chest, and {p2}'s glove bears no aconite.

clues.title: Gardening glove
clues.text: A glove of {p2}'s, with his initials, left beside the pots of aconite. He wore it to tend a plant before dinner.

clues.title: Register of movements
clues.text: {p2} and {p5} remained in {r3} from 21:10 to 21:25; both signed the register and a servant confirmed it.

clues.title: Clock and time register
clues.text: Clock checked: drink at 21:15, symptoms at 21:25, scream at 21:30. {p4} and {p3} remained in {r4} from 21:10 to 21:25; both signed the register and a servant confirmed it.

clues.title: Access register
clues.text: A servant saw {p1} enter {r1} at 21:15 with the drink and leave at 21:18. This contradicts her claim to have stayed in {r2}.

p1.text: I was alone in {r2} from 21:10 to 21:25. I did not enter {r1} during that time.
variants: I was alone in {r2} from 21:10 to 21:25. I did not enter {r1} during that time.
From 21:10 to 21:25 I remained in {r2}, alone. I shan't apologise for it, and I never set foot in {r1}.
Let me be perfectly clear: 21:10 to 21:25, in {r2}. Alone. Not in {r1}.

p1.text: My father and I disagreed over the inheritance. I had no wish to go on quarrelling with him.
variants: My father and I disagreed over the inheritance. I had no wish to go on quarrelling with him.
Let me be perfectly clear: my father and I did not agree about the inheritance. Don't mistake a disagreement for anything else.

p1.text: I received the notice: my father was to cut me out of the inheritance tomorrow. I signed the acknowledgement.
variants: I received the notice: my father was to cut me out of the inheritance tomorrow. I signed the acknowledgement.
Yes, my father was to disinherit me tomorrow, and I knew it: I signed for it. Don't twist my words: that is all I admit.

p1.text: The evidence ties me to the cup. I cannot maintain that I never touched it.
variants: The evidence ties me to the cup. I cannot maintain that I never touched it.
My fingerprint is on that cup, I see. I shan't deny what is plain to see.

p1.text: The register puts my entering {r1} at 21:15. My claim to have stayed in {r2} was false.
variants: The register puts my entering {r1} at 21:15. My claim to have stayed in {r2} was false.
Very well: at 21:15 I went into {r1} with the cup. I said I was in {r2}, and it was not true.

p1.text: I saw nothing out of the ordinary. I was alone.
variants: I saw nothing out of the ordinary. I was alone.
Nothing worth your attention. Had I seen anything, I would tell you.

p1.text: I am {p1}, the heiress of this house. You may begin your questions.
variants: I am {p1}, the heiress of this house. You may begin your questions.
My name is {p1}. I am the heiress; I imagine you've been told already.

p1.text: Let me be perfectly clear: I want this over quickly, and done properly. Ask.
variants: Let me be perfectly clear: I want this over quickly, and done properly. Ask.
Spare me the condolences. What exactly do you wish to establish?

p1.text: You will not put in my mouth an answer I don't have.
variants: You will not put in my mouth an answer I don't have.
I know nothing of that. Ask me something that is mine to answer.

p2.text: I was with {p5} in {r3} from 21:10 to 21:25. You may corroborate it.
variants: I was with {p5} in {r3} from 21:10 to 21:25. You may corroborate it.
From 21:10 to 21:25, {p5} and I were in {r3}. Two testimonies are worth more than one.

p2.text: Edmund asked me to go over his medical accounts. There was no debt outstanding.
variants: Edmund asked me to go over his medical accounts. There was no debt outstanding.
Let us be precise: I went over Edmund's medical accounts at his request. Nothing remained outstanding between us.

p2.text: I had corrected an error of addition in the medical accounts before handing them over.
variants: I had corrected an error of addition in the medical accounts before handing them over.
One must distinguish: correcting a sum is not fraud. Edmund accepted the correction and signed it.

p2.text: That print is not mine. I did not tamper with Edmund's drink.
variants: That print is not mine. I did not tamper with Edmund's drink.
Let us be precise: the analysis points to someone else, not to me.

p2.text: It is entered in the register: {p5} and I, in {r3}, from 21:10 to 21:25. More reliable than my memory.
variants: It is entered in the register: {p5} and I, in {r3}, from 21:10 to 21:25. More reliable than my memory.
We signed the register, and a servant confirms it. A register has no interest in the outcome.

p2.text: I was in {r3} with {p5}. Nobody else came in.
variants: I was in {r3} with {p5}. Nobody else came in.
With {p5}, in {r3}. No one crossed that threshold; I should have noticed.

p2.text: The glove is mine. I was in {r5} before dinner.
variants: The glove is mine. I was in {r5} before dinner.
Yes, that glove is mine. I wore it to tend a plant before dinner and left it there. One must distinguish: it was stained with nothing.

p2.text: I am Dr {p2}, the family doctor.
variants: I am Dr {p2}, the family doctor.
My name is {p2}. I have been the family doctor for many years. What do you wish to clarify?

p2.text: Let us be precise and brief. It has been a long night for everyone.
variants: Let us be precise and brief. It has been a long night for everyone.
Let us keep to the facts. Go ahead, ask.

p2.text: I have no information on which to state it.
variants: I have no information on which to state it.
On that I could only conjecture, and I do not conjecture.

p3.text: I was with {p4} in {r4} from 21:10 to 21:25. Ask, if you like.
variants: I was with {p4} in {r4} from 21:10 to 21:25. Ask, if you like.
I'll put it plainly: from 21:10 to 21:25, {p4} and I were in {r4}.

p3.text: My work depended on Sir Edmund. Ours was a working relationship.
variants: My work depended on Sir Edmund. Ours was a working relationship.
I worked for Sir Edmund. He was demanding and paid on time. That was enough for me.

p3.text: I kept back a letter applying for another post. I hadn't told Sir Edmund.
variants: I kept back a letter applying for another post. I hadn't told Sir Edmund.
I'll put it plainly: I was looking for another post and hadn't told Sir Edmund. That's all.

p3.text: I never touched that drink. The print isn't mine.
variants: I never touched that drink. The print isn't mine.
That evidence doesn't point to me. That's what I can tell you.

p3.text: Look at the register: {p4} and I, in {r4}, from 21:10 to 21:25.
variants: Look at the register: {p4} and I, in {r4}, from 21:10 to 21:25.
We both signed, and one of the servants saw us. It's a fact, not an opinion.

p3.text: I was in {r4} with {p4}. Only {p1} came in, at 21:12, to take the cup.
variants: I was in {r4} with {p4}. Only {p1} came in, at 21:12, to take the cup.
With {p4}, in {r4}. At 21:12 {p1} came by for the cup; nobody else.

p3.text: My name is {p3}. I'm Sir Edmund's secretary.
variants: My name is {p3}. I'm Sir Edmund's secretary.
I'm {p3}, secretary to Sir Edmund. Tell me what you need cleared up.

p3.text: Tell me what you need to know. I'll be brief.
variants: Tell me what you need to know. I'll be brief.
Ask whatever you like. I'll tell you what I know, and warn you when I'm only supposing.
I don't know.
I don't know, and I'd rather not guess.

p4.text: I was with {p3} in {r4} from 21:10 to 21:25, sir.
variants: I was with {p3} in {r4} from 21:10 to 21:25, sir.
If I may, I shall answer in order: from 21:10 to 21:25 I was in {r4}, in the company of {p3}.

p4.text: I had been thirty years in Sir Edmund's service. I preferred not to question his decisions.
variants: I had been thirty years in Sir Edmund's service. I preferred not to question his decisions.
Thirty years in Sir Edmund's service, sir. It was not my place to question his decisions.

p4.text: I meant to retire and had prepared a written request, sir.
variants: I meant to retire and had prepared a written request, sir.
My request to retire, sir. I had not yet submitted it. That is all on that point.

p4.text: That fingerprint is not mine, sir. I did not touch the drink after preparing it.
variants: That fingerprint is not mine, sir. I did not touch the drink after preparing it.
The evidence does not point to me, sir. That is all on that point.

p4.text: It is entered in the register, sir: {p3} and I, in {r4}, from 21:10 to 21:25.
variants: It is entered in the register, sir: {p3} and I, in {r4}, from 21:10 to 21:25.
We both signed the register, and a servant confirms it. In this house it is kept most scrupulously.

p4.text: I made the tea at 21:05, sir. {p1} took the cup away at 21:12.
variants: I made the tea at 21:05, sir. {p1} took the cup away at 21:12.
I was in {r4} with {p3}. Only {p1} came in, at 21:12, to take the cup.
With {p3}, in {r4}. At 21:12 {p1} came by for the cup; nobody else.
{p4}, butler of this house, sir.
My name is {p4}. I have been the butler these thirty years.

p4.text: Good evening, sir. I am listening.
variants: Good evening, sir. I am listening.
Let us keep the forms, though the night is against us. What do you wish to know?

p4.text: I could not inform you on that point, sir.
variants: I could not inform you on that point, sir.
It is not my place to know it, and I shall not presume.

p5.text: I was with {p2} in {r3} from 21:10 to 21:25. Go on, ask.
variants: I was with {p2} in {r3} from 21:10 to 21:25. Go on, ask.
{p2} and I were in {r3} from 21:10 to 21:25. Happy now?

p5.text: I owed my uncle money. We had a row before dinner was over.
variants: I owed my uncle money. We had a row before dinner was over.
I'll tell you straight: I owed him money and we had a row before dinner ended. Same as ever.

p5.text: I wanted to sell a family jewel to pay my debts. Hadn't sold it yet.
variants: I wanted to sell a family jewel to pay my debts. Hadn't sold it yet.
All right, yes: I was going to sell a family jewel to pay what I owe. I haven't sold it. Don't make a meal of it.

p5.text: Didn't touch that. The print's not mine, look.
variants: Didn't touch that. The print's not mine, look.
That evidence has nothing to do with me. Ask anyone you like.

p5.text: Look at the register: {p2} and me, in {r3}, from 21:10 to 21:25. All written down.
variants: Look at the register: {p2} and me, in {r3}, from 21:10 to 21:25. All written down.
We both signed and one of the servants saw us. What more do you want?

p5.text: I was in {r3} with {p2}. Nobody else came in.
variants: I was in {r3} with {p2}. Nobody else came in.
With {p2}, in {r3}. Not a soul came through that door.

p5.text: I'm {p5}, the nephew. The other Blackwood, the one nobody takes seriously.
variants: I'm {p5}, the nephew. The other Blackwood, the one nobody takes seriously.
{p5}. I'm the nephew, you know. What do you want to ask me?

p5.text: Come on, ask. The sooner we start, the sooner we're done.
variants: Come on, ask. The sooner we start, the sooner we're done.
What a night. What do you want to know?
I don't know.
No idea. And I'm not making something up just so you'll leave me alone.
